summary.oneLiner: Windlas Biotech is a Top-5 Indian Generic Formulations CDMO offering end-to-end formulation development, licensing and commercial manufacturing to leading pharmaceutical companies, alongside Trade Generics & Institutional and Exports verticals.
summary.business: Windlas Biotech Limited is a Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisation (CDMO) serving the generic formulations value chain, partnering with pharmaceutical companies (including 8 of the Top 10 Indian pharma companies) to develop, license and manufacture oral solid, liquid and injectable dosage forms across chronic and sub-chronic therapies. Beyond its core Generic Formulations CDMO vertical, it runs a Trade Generics & Institutional business distributing affordable medicines in Tier-2/Tier-3 India, and an Exports vertical serving international regulated and semi-regulated markets.

risks.note: Exposure to macroeconomic trends, regulatory changes and geopolitical factors; the Company relies on continuous monitoring and revenue diversification across its three business verticals and multiple geographies to manage this.

Manufacturing disruptions, cGMP compliance lapses or quality failures at any of its facilities could impair customer trust; mitigated through strict cGMP adherence, eQMS/LIMS systems and annual customer audits.
Domestic and international CDMO competition creates pricing pressure; the Company relies on economies of scale, customer partnerships and R&D-driven efficiency to compete.
API price volatility and supply-chain disruptions are flagged as a risk; mitigated via a diversified multi-geography supplier network and dual sourcing for critical APIs.
Export revenue is exposed to foreign-exchange volatility, managed through an internal framework and hedging strategy.

Tightening inspection norms and Schedule M compliance requirements could trigger regulatory action on specific product categories; the Company is investing in Schedule M-readiness across all facilities.

risks.risk: Customer concentration in the CDMO vertical
risks.note: Top-10 customers still account for 32% of Generic Formulations CDMO vertical revenue in FY26 (down from 52% in FY22), leaving meaningful reliance on a small set of large pharmaceutical customers despite the improving trend.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Windlas Biotech is a Top-5 Indian Generic Formulations CDMO offering end-to-end formulation development, licensing and commercial manufacturing to leading pharmaceutical companies, alongside Trade Generics & Institutional and Exports verticals.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Windlas Biotech Limited is a Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisation (CDMO) serving the generic formulations value chain, partnering with pharmaceutical companies (including 8 of the Top 10 Indian pharma companies) to develop, license and manufacture oral solid, liquid and injectable dosage forms across chronic and sub-chronic therapies. Beyond its core Generic Formulations CDMO vertical, it runs a Trade Generics & Institutional business distributing affordable medicines in Tier-2/Tier-3 India, and an Exports vertical serving international regulated and semi-regulated markets.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Windlas Inc. — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) non-operating US subsidiary; application for dissolution filed with the Delaware Division of Corporations on March 18, 2026, and the subsidiary was dissolved effective March 31, 2026
- US Pharma Windlas Inc. LLP — JV: Joint venture of the Company until July 12, 2024, after which the relationship ceased
- AKW WBL Family Private Trust — related party: Entity in which Key Managerial Personnel of the Company hold an interest

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: CDMO: INR664cr (20% YoY growth, 73% of revenue); Trade Generics: INR195cr (13% YoY growth, impacted by codeine syrup discontinuation); Exports: INR46cr (40% YoY growth, Q4 up 67% YoY to INR17cr); Injectables: commercialized in Philippines, EU-GMP readiness ongoing; Plant 6: mechanical completion achieved, H1FY27 commercialization target

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Generic Formulations CDMO:** Oral Solid Dosage forms, Liquid Dosage forms, Injectables (Ampoules, Vials, Lyophilised), modified-release products, chewables, dispersibles, complex generics, fixed-dose combinations
- **Trade Generics & Institutional:** affordable generic medicines distributed via Tier-2/Tier-3 network
- **Exports:** formulations exported to international regulated and semi-regulated markets

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic India (Tier-2/Tier-3 via Trade Generics)
- 10 countries markets (exports presence)
- United States (first product launch from Dehradun Plant-IV)
- South Africa (SAPHRA approval)
- Europe (EU-GMP approval)
- Philippines (GMP certification for Plant-4 & Plant-5)

certifications.title: Quality certifications
certifications.body:
- WHO-GMP (five manufacturing facilities)
- USFDA inspection clearance
- EU-GMP (Plant-IV, Europe)
- SAPHRA (South Africa, Plant-IV)
- GMP certification - Philippines (Plant-4 and Plant-5)
- DSIR-recognised R&D centre

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: no explicit guidance, but management expects continued growth across CDMO, Trade Generics, and Exports; margin: expects EBITDA to grow long-term; order inflow: no specific guidance; capex/commissioning: Plant 6 to be commercialized in H1FY27; no organic capex expected in FY27 beyond maintenance; next capex cycle may emerge in FY28 if utilization nears 60%

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Plant 6 (INR1000cr revenue potential excluding injectables); export market expansion via Philippines as gateway to ROW; GLP-1 vial filling capability in injectables plant; potential for new dosage forms (e.g., medicated chewing gums, chewables); institutional segment growth via government procurement programs

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's pharmaceutical market grew in value in FY26 even as industry unit volumes rose only ~2.7%; Windlas grew revenue 19%, outgrowing the market on a value basis
- Growth is led by chronic and sub-chronic therapies (cardiac, anti-diabetic, respiratory), which management flags as core to its CDMO therapy mix
- Structural shift of pharmaceutical companies outsourcing development and manufacturing to specialised CDMO partners; India's CDMO market is growing ~7-8% a year with India still holding only a low-single-digit share of the global market, implying a long runway
- A wave of patent expiries in India is expected to drive demand for generic and complex-generic launches, favouring companies with in-house IP-led formulation development and speed-to-market
- India's Trade Generics segment is seen as one of the fastest-structurally-expanding pharma segments, driven by affordability, deeper distribution and the government's Jan Aushadhi network
- Tightening regulatory standards (Schedule M / revised GMP norms) are pushing smaller, non-compliant manufacturers out of the market, which management expects to accelerate consolidation toward larger, quality-led CDMO players such as Windlas
- Rising incomes, widening insurance penetration and sustained government health investment are cited as durable macro tailwinds for pharmaceutical demand
- Management points to a growing development pipeline of complex generics, fixed-dose combinations and modified-release products, and describes plans for a first-to-launch pipeline in chronic therapy categories timed to the patent-expiry calendar, without disclosing pipeline size or order-book value

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 13.4% (FY26) and 13.6% (Q4); cost discipline maintained via automation, LMS-driven training, and working capital optimization; API price pressures observed but mitigated by diversified sourcing and low solvent dependency; no material margin compression expected

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritized buyback (INR47cr, no promoter participation); proposed dividend of INR13cr (INR6.3/share); balanced approach: growth investments (Plant 6) + shareholder returns; no M&A or debt-funded expansion planned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Windlas operates five WHO-GMP compliant manufacturing facilities in Dehradun spanning oral solids, liquids and injectables: Plant 1 (commissioned 2001, oral solids/liquids/pouches & sachets, established base capacity); Plant 2 (commissioned 2014, large-scale oral solids/liquids/sachets, including a Plant-2 extension completed in FY25); Plant 3 (commissioned 2018, oral solids - tablets & capsules); Plant 4 (commissioned 2009, oral solids - tablets/capsules/sachets, received Philippines GMP certification in FY26); Plant 5 (commissioned 2024, injectables - ampoules, vials, lyophilised, received Philippines GMP certification in FY26); and Plant 6 (brownfield OSD expansion at Selaqui, in progress - mechanical completion achieved in FY26, commercialisation on track for H1 FY27). Capacity utilisation rose to 66% in FY26 from 59% in FY25, and the gross block of fixed assets increased to Rs.4,262 million from Rs.3,512 million. Earlier capex milestones cited in the Company's journey include Rs.89 million invested in plant and machinery expansion (2019-20), scaling capsule and tablet manufacturing capacity from 5+ billion to 7+ billion units by March 2022, completion of the Plant-II expansion in FY25, and initiation of capex for OSD capacity expansion at Plant-VI in FY25. The Company also operates a DSIR-approved R&D centre with pilot-scale facilities, with R&D spend rising 32% YoY to Rs.83 million in FY26.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, disciplined, long-term oriented; emphasized operational excellence, capital efficiency, and quality-by-design; avoided guidance but expressed strong conviction in export and injectables growth; highlighted culture of compliance and talent retention

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Partnerships with 8 of the Top 10 Indian pharmaceutical companies and 926 CDMO customers served
- Formulation expertise and intellectual-property-led product development — the Company develops and owns the IP behind the formulations it makes, unlike a build-to-spec model
- Flexible manufacturing infrastructure spanning oral solids, liquids and injectables enabling speed, scalability and cost competitiveness in complex generics
- Extensive distribution network for Trade Generics & Institutional reaching Tier-2/Tier-3 and underserved healthcare markets
- Deep portfolio in complex generics, fixed-dose combinations and modified-release products positioned to capture patent-expiry driven demand
- Track record of thirteen consecutive quarters of record revenue, evidencing execution consistency and customer trust

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Regulatory scrutiny intensifying (Schedule M, EU-GMP, FDA); codeine syrup discontinuation impact lingering; export revenue volatility due to long approval cycles; GLP-1 market adoption uncertain; API supply chain disruptions; potential margin pressure from competitive pricing in trade generics

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: 70-80 customer audits/year across 4 plants — a rare operational discipline in Indian pharma; electronic LMS for SOP training with 80% pass threshold — unique in Indian CDMO space; Plant 6’s INR1000cr potential excludes injectables, implying even higher total capacity; export growth is binary but high-margin, with Philippines approval as strategic gateway to Africa/SEA

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Complete the commissioning of Plant-6 and integrate it into digital planning and QMS systems from day one
- Deploy Plant-6 capacity across all three business verticals to reduce lead times and improve customer responsiveness
- Scale up injectables across all three business verticals
- Deepen customer relationships in CDMO — deepen wallet share with existing marquee customers and add new accounts, especially in value-added segments
- Continue providing Accessible, Affordable and Authentic medication to underserved regions and add more Institutional accounts
- Extend export reach in markets where the …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Product discontinuation] "The Trade Generics & Institutional vertical reported revenue of Rs 30 crore, following the discontinuation of codeine-based products. As we expand the portfolio with new launches and replacements, we expect to progressively bridge the gap." This vertical is the one segment shown declining (-32% in the Q1 mix chart) against a long-run FY22-FY26 revenue CAGR of +29%.
- [ESOP accounting] ESOP charge is a material non-cash P&L item - Rs 7.16 Cr in Q1FY27 and Rs 17 Cr in FY26 (vs Rs 2 Cr in FY25) - and the deck publishes a half-yearly expected schedule out to FY2030-31 (ESOP Plan 2025, ESOS Plan 2023, ESOP Plan 2021), declining over time. All reported vs adjusted metrics in the deck differ by this item.
- [Industry backdrop] "The Indian Pharmaceutical Market (IPM) witnessed a volume growth of 3.4% in Q1 FY27, reflecting a steady yet measured industry environment."
- [Portfolio history] Milestones note the divestment of Windlas Healthcare to Cadila Healthcare (2018 block) and the earlier acquisition of the erstwhile associate Windlas Healthcare, now Plant-4; also an investment of Rs 75 Cr from Tano India Private Equity Fund II, and listing on the exchanges in August 2021.
- [Policy tailwind] Trade Generics opportunity cites "Policy Support: Government initiatives (e.g., Jan Aushadhi Yojana) encouraging trade generic adoption" and "Untapped Rural Demand".
